failure_modes: Insufficient analytical sensitivity on low-biomass capture-eluted fractions leading to inconsistent or non-reproducible peroxidation/permeability signals even when functional/capture loss is present (false negatives).

Assay signal driven by co-isolated soluble lipid complexes, lipoproteins, or other non-vesicular lipid particles in the capture-positive fraction rather than EV membranes — causing signals that do not reflect EV integrity and decoupling chemistry readouts from capture/protection loss (false positives).

Fluorescent reporters or colorimetric reagents (BODIPY C11, TBARS reagents, permeability dyes) are interfered with by capture-elution buffers, formulation excipients (e.g., surfactants), or device residues, producing artifactual oxidation or dye uptake signals that do not reflect membrane chemistry.

Spike-in recovery controls fail to detect matrix-dependent assay suppression or enhancement because the tracer is not isomorphic in membrane composition/packing to the test EVs, producing misleading validation of assay performance.

Observed chemistry changes (even if real and reproducible) do not predict in vivo delivery or biodistribution failures due to species- or route-specific clearance/retention mechanisms (i.e., lipid-oxidation/permeability is necessary but not sufficient to predict translational exposure outcomes).

The proposed qualitative pass/fail thresholds cannot be defined robustly across lots because baseline variability in lipid oxidation/permeability between donor lots, culture conditions, or capture efficiency is high, preventing discrimination of true failures from normal lot-to-lot noise.

Material limits prevent LC-MS confirmation of oxidized phospholipids in the fraction, leaving only lower-specificity assays (BODIPY/TBARS) and reducing confidence in the chemical identity of the signal.

Contradictory preclinical delivery evidence (rodent intranasal efficacy vs. primate intranasal failure-to-detect) undermines the assumption that early chemical flags of membrane damage will meaningfully de-risk intranasal bridging studies — i.e., even chemically intact EVs may fail to deliver in large animals or humans.
strongest_objection: The single strongest bounded risk is that the proposed chemistry-centered readouts (BODIPY C11, TBARS, permeability dyes, targeted oxPL LC-MS) will either (A) lack sufficient sensitivity and specificity on the very low-biomass, capture-eluted fractions to produce reproducible, discriminating signals, or (B) report signals that arise from co-isolated non-EV lipid-containing material or assay-interfering excipients rather than bona fide EV membrane damage. Either outcome would make the chemistry readouts uninformative: they would not track with loss of capture/protection signatures (false negatives if insensitive; false positives if driven by co-isolates/excipients) and therefore would not be useful as stability-indicating gates prior to resource-intensive potency/bridging studies. This bounded failure unifies assay-performance, fraction-purity, and formulation-interference risks and directly undermines the proposal’s causal claim that measured lipid chemistry changes are mechanistically upstream and predictive of functional loss.
